body: Mathematician (codebreaker, Chern-Simons) who founded Renaissance Technologies (1982). Medallion fund, per Zuckerman's The Man Who Solved the Market: ~66% gross / ~39% net a year 1988-2018, ~$104.5bn of trading profits, fees of 5% of assets plus up to 44% of profits. Medallion has been closed to outsiders for decades and capped (~$10bn) because its edge is capacity-limited. Structural edge: decades of cleaned data, hundreds of PhD scientists (not finance people), huge compute, very short holding periods, thousands of small statistically weak but persistent signals, high leverage, and extreme secrecy. Its public funds (e.g., RIEF) did far worse - reportedly lost ~20-30% in 2020 while Medallion gained (figures unverified) - proof the edge does not scale to longer horizons. Mistake/near-death: Medallion's early years (1989) had a large drawdown that led Simons to rebuild the models with Berlekamp (unverified detail). Simons died in May 2024. Lesson for an individual: this is the clearest example of an edge that cannot be copied; anyone selling 'Medallion-like' retail algos is misleading. What can be copied is the attitude: trust data over stories, kill signals that stop working, and let the system (not emotions) execute.

data.copyable: systematic rules, data over narrative; NOT the returns
data.edge_structural: data, scientists, compute, short horizon, leverage, capacity cap
data.track_record: 66% gross / 39% net 1988-2018 (Zuckerman; Cornell 2020 paper questions how)

title: Jim Simons - Renaissance Medallion (the uncopyable edge)
